channel.title: The Wilson Times - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Wilson Times (wilsontimes.com)

item.title: For Your Health: Building healthy habits for a healthy heart
item.description: American Heart Month highlights how managing blood pressure and cholesterol, eating well, exercising and knowing heart attack symptoms can help prevent much of heart disease.

item.title: Greenfield boys grab 4th place at NCISAA Div. III swim meet
item.description: Greenfield boys rode top-four relays and Gabriel Navarro’s double fourths to 4th place at the NCISAA Div. III meet, while the girls finished 12th behind Shelby Vester and two scoring relays.

item.title: How low can he go?
item.description: After Trump's Super Bowl meme depicting the Obamas as chimps and autocratic talk, a North Carolina pastor warns of his mental decline, threats to democracy and why the midterm vote now underway matters.

item.title: Target needs to kick ICE out of its stores
item.description: After Border Patrol agents assaulted and detained two U.S. citizens in a Minnesota Target, an op-ed says the retailer’s ICE ties have sparked nationwide protests and demands that it end cooperation with immigration authorities.

item.title: How concerned are you?
item.description: Amid rising pessimism about America’s future, Tom Campbell looks to North Carolina’s primary turnout as a test of how concerned citizens are — and urges voters to rally others to the polls.

item.title: Bigger Congress would be better Congress
item.description: Columnist John Hood argues the U.S. House is far too small and should add seats, saying a larger chamber would improve representation, curb gerrymandering and boost states like North Carolina.

item.title: Our Opinion: Sheriff showdowns, Dem congressional clash on the ballot
item.description: Wilson County’s March 6 primaries feature crowded sheriff races, a Democratic challenger contest for Rep. Greg Murphy and U.S. Senate and court seats on the ballot.

item.title: Thank you, Buck Newton
item.description: A letter credits state Sen. Buck Newton for school vouchers, declining public school funding, looser gun and abortion rules, gerrymandering and greater secrecy in North Carolina politics.

item.title: Elm City awards lift station rehab contract
item.description: Elm City commissioners gave the OK to award a $599,000 contract with Ed Braswell & Sons to rehabilitate lift stations with ARPA funds, restoring them to original performance and adding state-required monitoring.
